title: Abyss Expedition on Android: AI-assisted development with bundled HTML/CSS/JS
author: Alarmed-Tailor1681
selftext:
I'm the developer of Abyss Expedition, a free Android roguelite. You draw equipment from a loot board, see what remains, and choose whether to draw again, clear the board for supplies and an expedition upgrade, or switch boards under the game's conditions and costs. Then you equip the results and head into the dungeon.



Development uses AI-assisted coding and generated images. The game UI and logic are HTML/CSS/JavaScript, packaged with Capacitor. One concrete constraint in this project is keeping the generated bundle and the prepared native asset copies consistent. Common changes go through a regeneration-and-sync step with file comparisons. That step prepares the files; getting a change into an installed app still requires a new native build and release.



The artwork also affects how I approach UI changes. The buttons and slots have painted frames, so the project rule is to inspect each individual frame at 360x800 and 390x844. A centered wrapper or matching DOM coordinates alone doesn't establish that the text looks centered inside the painted opening. A single displaced label gets a correction scoped to that label.



For other people using AI to build a bundled mobile game, how do you keep the screen you inspect and the files in the installed app in sync?



Android Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.songistore.abyssexpedition&hl=en&referrer=utm\_source%3Daigamedev%26utm\_medium%3Dorganic\_post%26utm\_campaign%3Dandroid\_growth\_20261014](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.songistore.abyssexpedition&hl=en&referrer=utm_source%3Daigamedev%26utm_medium%3Dorganic_post%26utm_campaign%3Dandroid_growth_20261014)
